## 一、核心概括

澳门第13/2023号法律《金融体系法律制度》确立“许可经营+持续监管”双轨框架：任何机构须获许可方可在澳经营金融业务，仅信用机构可吸收公众存款；澳门金融管理局（AMCM）负责制定审慎规章并行使监管、协调及监察职权。以下从准入、业务边界、监管职权、规章体系、机构范围及退出监管六方面展开。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 准入许可制度：未经许可不得经营

**法规出处**：中国澳门《金融体系法律制度》第4条第1款、第4款【来源5】。

**深度解读**：该条确立金融业“许可保留”原则——只有依本法或专有法规获许可的金融机构，方可在澳门经营金融业务。立法意图在于将金融活动纳入事前准入控制，防止无资质主体从事高风险业务。第4款针对未经许可经营者设置严厉后果：AMCM可声请法院命令解散及司法清算，即不仅行政处罚，更可直接诉请消灭主体资格，体现对非法金融活动的零容忍。

**重点提示**：判断是否构成“经营金融业务”须结合第4条第2款列举的十二类活动（接受存款、批给贷款、支付服务、发行支付工具、金融工具交易、承销分销、货币经纪、资产管理、风险投资、保险再保险、退休基金管理及AMCM通告订定的其他业务），以“惯常或营利方式”从事即触发许可要求。偶发、非营利行为一般不落入规制范围。

**实务指引**：拟在澳展业者应先对照第4条第2款逐项自查业务是否落入列举范围；若属边缘业务，可事先向AMCM咨询或申请认定。切勿以“咨询公司”“科技公司”名义实质从事支付、资产管理等业务，否则面临解散清算风险。申请许可需准备公司章程、股东及主要出资人资信材料、业务计划、风控与合规架构等。

### 2. 存款业务专属信用机构

**法规出处**：中国澳门《金融体系法律制度》第4条第3款【来源5】；第3条第1款第（一）项【来源4】。

**深度解读**：第4条第3款明确“仅信用机构方可经营接受公众存款或其他应偿还款项的业务”，这是金融体系中最重要的业务边界。信用机构依第3条第1款第（一）项包括银行、有限制业务银行及邮政储金局。立法意图在于保护存款人——吸收公众资金具有系统重要性，须由资本充足、受审慎监管的信用机构专营。其他金融机构（金融公司、兑换店、融资租赁公司等）虽可从事贷款、支付等业务，但不得吸收公众存款。

**重点提示**：判断“公众存款”的核心是向不特定公众吸收资金并承诺偿还，无论名目为“理财”“保证金”还是“预付款”。变相吸存是常见违规形态。此外，第3条第2款指出邮政储金局及第（二）至（十二）项机构由专有法规规范，适用时须叠加对应专门法。

**实务指引**：非信用机构设计产品时应避免任何承诺还本付息的公众资金归集安排；与信用机构合作代销时须厘清资金流向，确保不构成实质吸存。信用机构则须持续满足资本充足及流动性要求，并注意存款保障相关专有法规的衔接。

### 3. AMCM的监管职权与持续监管

**法规出处**：中国澳门《金融体系法律制度》第7条【来源3】。

**深度解读**：第7条构建AMCM作为监管当局的职权体系：第1款为监管、协调及监察的一般职权；第2款列举五项具体职责——监督法律规章遵守、确保机构健全谨慎管理、促进良好操守与高透明度营商、对不当情事发出警告并命令补正、遏止与机构性质不符或影响市场正常运作的做法。第3款尤为关键：即使机构许可失效、被废止或业务中止终止，AMCM仍保留监管职责直至所有债权人获清偿或清算程序终止，实现“监管不留真空”。

**重点提示**：第2款第（四）项的“警告并命令补正”属行政监管措施，可与行政处罚并行；机构收到补正命令后须在指定期限内整改，逾期可能触发更严厉措施。第3款意味着退出阶段的清算、债权清偿仍在监管视野内，清算人须与AMCM保持沟通。

**实务指引**：金融机构应建立与AMCM的常态化沟通机制，及时报告重大事项；收到警告或补正命令后应立即启动内部整改并留存证据。拟退出市场的机构须提前规划清算方案，确保债权人清偿过程符合监管要求，避免在清算期间擅自处置资产。

### 4. AMCM的规章制定权：审慎监管规则体系

**法规出处**：中国澳门《金融体系法律制度》第8条【来源2】。

**深度解读**：第8条授权AMCM以通告或传阅文件订定属其职责范围的规章，尤其涵盖六类事项：资本充足规则、风险管理规则、公司治理规则、业务经营规则、讯息披露及审计规则，以及旨在保障金融体系整体稳定及有效运作的其他谨慎规则。这构成澳门金融审慎监管的“二级立法”基础——法律定框架，AMCM以通告填充技术标准。该条同时规定金融公司章程修改（所营事业、公司名称、公司机关、住所、公司资本）须取得AMCM预先许可，名称变更由AMCM以通告在《澳门特别行政区公报》公布。

**重点提示**：AMCM通告具有普遍约束力，机构须持续跟踪其更新，尤其是资本充足与风险管理指标可能随市场变化调整。章程修改的预先许可属事前审批，未获许可的修改不产生效力；名称变更还须经公报公布程序。

**实务指引**：金融机构应指定专人跟踪AMCM通告及传阅文件动态，建立“规章—内部制度”映射表，定期比对更新内部政策。章程修改前先向AMCM提交申请并取得预先许可，再办理商业登记及公报公布手续。审计与讯息披露须按AMCM规则准备材料，确保报送及时、准确。

### 5. 金融机构的范围与专有法规衔接

**法规出处**：中国澳门《金融体系法律制度》第3条【来源4】。

**深度解读**：第3条第1款以列举方式界定十三类金融机构，涵盖信用机构、金融公司、风险资本公司、现金速递公司、兑换店、财产管理公司、投资基金管理公司、融资租赁公司、保险公司、再保险公司、退休基金管理公司、法律订定的其他机构，以及AMCM认定并经行政长官许可的其他机构。第2款明确邮政储金局及第（二）至（十二）项机构由专有法规规范，即本法为一般法，专有法规为特别法，适用时特别法优先。第3款则规定第（十三）项机构适用经适当配合后的第二编及第四编第二章。

**重点提示**：机构类型决定其可从事的业务范围与适用法规层级。例如保险公司主要适用保险专有法规，本法仅作补充；而AMCM认定类机构须经行政长官许可，程序更为严格。第（十三）项的“兜底”设计为新型金融业态预留准入通道。

**实务指引**：设立机构前应先确定拟采用的组织形式对应第3条哪一项，进而识别应适用的专有法规及许可程序。对创新型业务，可评估是否申请第（十三）项认定。集团化经营时须注意不同牌照对应不同监管要求，避免跨牌照违规经营。

### 6. 适用范围除外与监管边界

**法规出处**：中国澳门《金融体系法律制度》第1条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：第1条界定本法适用范围为在澳门特别行政区经营金融业务的法律制度，同时第2款排除三类活动：澳门特区从事的财政活动（邮政储金局除外）、特区参加的国际组织依章程从事的金融活动、押店的当押活动。立法意图在于划清金融监管与公共财政、国际组织特权及传统典当业的边界，避免监管重叠。

**重点提示**：押店当押活动虽不适用本法，但不等于完全不受规制，其仍受专门法规约束；邮政储金局在财政活动中被特别保留在本法框架内，体现其金融属性。国际组织豁免须以章程规定为依据，不得类推扩大。

**实务指引**：涉及特区财政或国际组织金融活动的主体，应先确认是否落入第1条第2款除外情形，避免误判而遗漏许可申请。押店经营者应关注当押专有法规而非本法。对边界模糊的业务，建议向AMCM书面咨询确认适用性。

## 三、总结与建议

澳门《金融体系法律制度》以**许可准入**为门槛、以**AMCM持续监管**为核心、以**审慎规章体系**为技术支撑，构建了覆盖机构准入、业务边界、公司治理、讯息披露到退出清算的全周期监管框架。核心行动指引：一是展业前对照第4条自查业务是否需许可，存款业务仅限信用机构；二是持续跟踪AMCM依第8条发布的通告，动态更新合规制度；三是章程修改等事项须事前取得AMCM许可。

延伸提醒：第一，第7条第3款的“退出后监管”意味着清算阶段仍须配合AMCM，不可擅自了结；第二，第3条机构分类决定适用专有法规，混业经营须逐牌照合规；第三，第1条除外情形有限，勿以“非金融”名义规避许可，否则面临第4条第4款解散清算风险。建议建立与AMCM的常态化沟通及法规跟踪机制。

## 一、核心概括

美国对政府通讯截取与监控的限制主要来源于**联邦宪法第四修正案**的判例体系、**《外国情报监视法》（FISA）** 及其特别法庭审查机制，以及**《电子通讯隐私法》（ECPA）** 等成文法。核心逻辑是：政府监控须以**令状原则**为基础，受**司法审查**约束，并区分刑事侦查与国家安全两种场景适用不同标准。需说明的是，您提供的参考资料主要涉及电信营销与设施安全领域，与政府监控限制的直接关联有限，以下分析将结合美国该领域公认的成文法框架展开，并对资料可支撑部分予以标注。


## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 宪法第四修正案的令状原则与合理隐私期待

**法规出处**：美国联邦宪法第四修正案（U.S. Const. amend. IV）；相关判例体系（Katz v. United States, 389 U.S. 347 (1967) 等）。

**深度解读**：第四修正案禁止"无理搜查与扣押"，要求政府监控须具备**合理根据（probable cause）** 并取得司法令状。Katz案确立的"合理隐私期待"标准，将通讯内容纳入保护范围——政府截取通话内容原则上须事先获得法官授权的令状。该原则构成美国监控法律体系的宪法底线，成文法（如ECPA、FISA）均是其具体化。

**重点提示**：令状原则存在例外，如**同意监控**、**紧急情况**、**一方同意录音**（各州规定不一，部分州要求双方同意）。

**实务指引**：企业若涉及员工通讯监控，应事先取得书面同意并制定明确政策；跨境业务中需注意美国执法机构依据令状向美国境内服务商调取数据的可能性。

> 说明：您提供的参考资料未包含第四修正案条文或相关判例原文，上述内容基于美国宪法通识框架，供方向性参考。

### 2. 《外国情报监视法》（FISA）与外国情报监视法庭（FISC）

**法规出处**：美国《Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978》，50 U.S.C. § 1801 et seq.；设立**外国情报监视法庭（FISC）** 进行秘密审查。

**深度解读**：FISA针对**国家安全目的**的电子监控设立专门程序：政府须向FISC申请令状，证明监控对象为"外国势力代理人"且监控目的为获取外国情报。与刑事令状相比，FISA令状标准较低、程序保密，但受FISC及**外国情报监视复审法庭（FISCR）** 审查。2008年《FISA修正案》（Section 702）进一步允许对境外非美国人的通讯进行定向收集。

**重点提示**：Section 702收集的美国境内"附带收集"数据引发持续争议；美国公民享有额外保护，但实践中边界复杂。

**实务指引**：跨国企业应评估其通讯是否可能落入FISA收集范围，对敏感数据传输采取加密与最小化措施。

> 说明：参考资料库未收录FISA条文，上述为美国该领域基础框架，具体适用请以现行法条为准。

### 3. 《电子通讯隐私法》（ECPA）与《存储通讯法》（SCA）

**法规出处**：美国《Electronic Communications Privacy Act of 1986》，18 U.S.C. § 2510–2523（截取）及§ 2701–2713（存储通讯）。

**深度解读**：ECPA禁止故意截取电子通讯，政府须依令状或法定例外方可进行；SCA规范政府向服务商调取**存储数据**，按数据新旧与性质适用不同令状标准（如180天以上存储邮件的历史上适用较低标准，后经判例与立法调整）。该法构成美国刑事侦查中通讯监控的主要成文法依据。

**重点提示**：ECPA对"实时截取"与"存储调取"区分严格，程序瑕疵可能导致证据排除。

**实务指引**：云服务企业应建立执法请求响应流程，区分传票（subpoena）、法院命令（court order）与搜查令（warrant）的适用层级。

> 说明：参考资料库未收录ECPA条文，上述为美国该领域基础框架。

### 4. 州法不冲突原则的参照意义

**法规出处**：美国《Customer Proprietary Network Information (CPNI)》64.2502【来源1】；《Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards》27.405【来源3】。

**深度解读**：来源1规定联邦CPNI规则**不优先（shall not preempt）** 某些要求政府实体与运营商签订合同以限制其获取电信服务的州法；来源3则确立联邦化学品设施安全规则对**冲突州法**的优先效力。二者共同体现美国联邦制下"联邦—州"权限划分逻辑：监控领域同样存在联邦标准与州宪法/州法更高保护并存的现象（如部分州对通讯记录有更严格令状要求）。

**重点提示**：州法不得与联邦监控法冲突，但可提供**更强隐私保护**；企业须同时评估联邦与运营地州法。

**实务指引**：在多州运营的通讯相关企业，应制作"联邦—州合规矩阵"，识别各州对政府数据请求的额外程序要求。

### 5. 电信营销规则中的通讯限制参照

**法规出处**：美国《Telemarketing Sales Rule (TSR)》310.1【来源4】、310.4【来源2】。

**深度解读**：来源4明确TSR实施《Telemarketing and Consumer Fraud and Abuse Prevention Act》（15 U.S.C. 6101–6108）；来源2详细规定**呼叫时间限制**（仅限当地时间8:00–21:00）、**禁止骚扰性重复呼叫**、**放弃呼叫（abandoned call）不超过3%**、**预先录制信息须获书面同意**等。这些规则虽针对商业营销而非政府监控，但体现美国对"通讯侵扰"的成文法限制思路，可作为理解通讯自由边界的参照。

**重点提示**：来源2的310.4(b)(1)(iii)明确"do-not-call"登记与例外（书面同意或既有业务关系），程序合规要求严格。

**实务指引**：涉及电话外呼的企业应建立书面同意档案、呼叫时段控制与放弃率监测系统。

> 说明：上述规则针对商业电话营销，**不直接规范政府监控行为**，仅作制度参照。


## 三、总结与建议

美国对政府通讯截取与监控的限制，核心是**宪法第四修正案的令状原则**，辅以**FISA**（国家安全场景）与**ECPA/SCA**（刑事侦查场景）的成文法程序，并由**FISC等司法机构**审查。联邦与州法并存，州法可提供更强保护但不得与联邦法冲突（参照来源1、来源3的优先效力逻辑）。**行动指引**：企业应建立执法请求分级响应机制、跨境数据传输加密与最小化策略，并制作联邦—州合规矩阵。

**延伸提醒**：
1. 您提供的参考资料主要覆盖电信营销（TSR）与设施安全（CFATS）领域，**未直接收录FISA、ECPA条文**，涉及具体监控合规时请以现行成文法与判例为准。
2. 关注Section 702的国会重新授权动态及FISC判例更新。
3. 跨境业务须同时评估美国执法调取与母国数据出境法的冲突。

1.985 Form, notice of, and conduct of hearing.
(a)
After an employee requests a hearing, the hearing official or administrative law judge shall notify the employee of the form of the hearing to be provided. If the hearing will be oral, the notice shall set forth the date, time, and location for the hearing. If the hearing will be paper, the employee shall be notified that he or she should submit his or her position and arguments in writing to the hearing official or administrative law judge by a specified date after which the record shall be closed. This date shall give the employee reasonable time to submit this information.

(b)
An employee who requests an oral hearing shall be provided an oral hearing if the hearing official or administrative law judge determines that the matter cannot be resolved by review of documentary evidence, for example, when an issue of credibility or veracity is involved. If a determination is made to provide an oral hearing, the hearing official or administrative law judge may offer the employee the opportunity for a hearing by telephone conference call. If this offer is rejected or if the hearing official or administrative law judge declines to offer a telephone conference call hearing, the employee shall be provided an oral hearing permitting the personal appearance of the employee, his or her personal representative, and witnesses.

 A record or transcript of every oral hearing shall be made. Witnesses shall testify under oath or affirmation. VA shall not be responsible for the payment of any expenses incident to attendance at the hearing which are incurred by either the employee, his or her representative or Counsel, or witnesses.

(c)
In all other cases where an employee requests a hearing, a paper hearing shall be provided. A paper hearing shall consist of a review of the written evidence of record by the administrative law judge or hearing official.
(d)
In any hearing under this section, the administrative law judge or hearing official may exclude from consideration evidence or testimony which is irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly repetitious.

## 一、核心概括

美国电子商务消费者保护并非由单一法律集中规制，而是通过**电子签名效力认定、预付费账户信息披露、电话营销行为规制**等多部联邦法规协同实现。核心机制包括：赋予电子签名与电子记录同等法律效力、强制交易前费用披露、禁止滥用性营销行为，以及通过消费者同意和记录保存义务强化问责。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 电子签名与电子记录的法律效力认定

**法规出处**：美国联邦法规第47编《Universal Service》§54.1812及§54.419【来源1】【来源3】

**深度解读**：两部法规均援引《全球及国内商务电子签名法》（E-Sign Act）的定义，明确电子签名——即"附着于或逻辑关联于合同或其他记录、由本人以签署意图执行或采用的电子声音、符号或过程"——具有与手写签名**同等法律效力**；电子记录亦构成合法"记录"。这一制度安排是电子商务消费者保护的**基础性前提**：只有电子合同、电子确认、电子授权具备法律效力，后续的知情权、同意权、救济权才有实现的载体。立法意图在于消除交易形式的不确定性，使消费者在线完成的注册、认证、授权等行为获得与纸质交易同等的保护力度。

**重点提示**：电子签名效力并非绝对——其适用范围受具体法规限定（"For the purposes of this..."），且需满足"签署意图"要件。在涉及资格认证等场景中，法规要求电子签名须**独立于其他协议或表格**、单独签署，防止捆绑授权。

**实务指引**：企业应确保电子签名流程可追溯（保留时间戳、IP记录、操作日志）；认证类文件须单独成表、单独签署，不得与其他条款混同；建议在用户界面明确提示"点击即构成法律签署"。

### 2. 交易前信息披露义务——预付费账户的强制披露规则

**法规出处**：美国联邦法规第12编《Regulation E》§1005.18【来源4】

**深度解读**：该条构建了预付费账户（prepaid account）**取得前**（pre-acquisition）的强制性披露体系，是电子商务消费者知情权的典型制度设计。核心要求包括：**短表披露**须列明周期性费用、单次购买费、ATM取现费（网络内/外两档）、现金充值费、余额查询费、客服费、不活跃费等，并以表格形式呈现；**长表披露**须列明全部可能收取的费用及收取条件。披露须在消费者取得账户**之前**完成，零售场景下可豁免长表前置但须在包装外表面提供短表并告知获取长表的电话和网址。法规还对字体大小（如单笔费用最低15磅）、颜色对比、分组顺序作出精确规定，并禁止在短表中披露第三方费用（现金充值费除外）。

**重点提示**：若消费者通过电子方式取得账户，披露须以**可机读、可跨屏幕尺寸查看、支持屏幕阅读器**的电子形式提供；多服务计划场景下须以分栏表格披露各计划费用；费用变动须在24个月内重新评估并更新披露。

**实务指引**：企业应建立费用披露模板并定期复核（至少每24个月）；电商平台销售预付费类产品时，须确保披露在购买确认页面前展示；保留披露版本的历史记录以备监管核查；外语营销场景下须提供对应语种的交易前披露。

### 3. 电话营销中的滥用行为禁止与消费者同意机制

**法规出处**：美国联邦法规第16编《Telemarketing Sales Rule》§310.4【来源5】

**深度解读**：该条是电子商务营销环节消费者保护的核心规范，禁止一系列**滥用性电话营销行为**，包括：威胁恐吓或使用污秽语言；就信用修复服务在结果达成前收费；就债务减免服务在重新协商成功且消费者完成至少一笔付款前收费；未经明示知情同意即提交账单信息扣款；使用远程创建支付指令或现金到现金转账作为支付方式；未向来电显示服务传输真实号码和名称等。其中**"预获账户信息"**（preacquired account information）场景要求尤为严格：涉及"免费转付费"转换的，须获取账户后四位数字、消费者明示同意，并**全程录音**；其他预获信息场景须具体标识扣款账户并取得明示同意。

**重点提示**：呼叫时间限于被叫方当地时间**早8点至晚9点**；弃呼率不得超过3%；录音须完整保存；"签名"包括符合联邦或州合同法的电子签名。违反者面临联邦贸易委员会执法及民事处罚。

**实务指引**：电商企业开展电话营销或电话确认订单时，应建立书面合规程序、培训人员、维护内部"勿扰"名单并每31天更新联邦勿扰登记库数据；涉及预获账户信息的交易须完整录音并保存；支付方式应避免使用现金到现金转账或远程创建支付指令。

### 4. 注册与认证信息的收集、传输与保密义务

**法规出处**：美国联邦法规第47编《Customer Proprietary Network Information》§64.611【来源2】

**深度解读**：该条虽主要规范互联网中继服务（TRS）注册，但其体现的**"收集—告知—同意—传输—保密"**五步框架对电子商务消费者信息保护具有参照意义。核心要求：服务商须在获取用户同意前，以**清晰易懂的语言**描述将被传输的具体信息、传输目的（确保项目正当管理）、以及拒绝同意的后果（拒绝服务）；须取得并保存用户**肯定性确认**的记录；对注册和认证信息负有**保密义务**，除法律或法规要求外不得披露。此外，法规对身份验证前的服务窗口（最长两周）、号码保留期（最长30天）等设定了明确时限。

**重点提示**：同意必须是"肯定性确认"（affirmative acknowledgment），默示同意不满足要求；保密义务为持续性义务，不因服务终止而消灭；信息传输须按数据库管理员规定的格式进行。

**实务指引**：电商平台收集消费者个人信息用于第三方传输时，应设计独立的同意勾选界面（非预勾选），用平实语言说明信息用途和拒绝后果；保存同意记录至少与业务关系存续期一致；建立信息访问权限控制和泄露应急机制。

### 5. 违规后果与消费者救济路径

**法规出处**：综合上述法规的执法机制【来源4】【来源5】

**深度解读**：美国电子商务消费者保护的执行呈现**多头执法**特征：联邦贸易委员会（FTC）负责《电话营销销售规则》的执法，违规行为可被认定为"不公平或欺骗性行为"，面临民事罚款和禁令；消费者金融保护局（CFPB）负责《Regulation E》的执行，预付费账户披露违规可导致行政处罚和消费者赔偿；联邦通信委员会（FCC）负责通信相关规则的执行。消费者个人亦可通过民事诉讼寻求救济，尤其在电子资金转账未经授权的情形下，§1005.18(e)设定了**责任限额和错误解决程序**——但未完成身份验证的账户不享受该等保护。

**重点提示**：未验证账户（unverified account）在责任限额和错误解决方面**不受保护**，这是消费者需特别注意的风险点；错误解决的60天报告期限起算点与电子访问或书面历史发送时间挂钩。

**实务指引**：企业应建立内部投诉处理和错误解决流程，确保在法定期限内响应；对未验证账户须以显著方式披露风险；保留所有交易历史和费用汇总记录（法规要求显示上月及本年度累计费用总额）。

## 三、总结与建议

美国电子商务消费者保护的核心逻辑是**"形式效力保障＋事前信息披露＋行为负面清单＋信息处理规范"**四位一体：电子签名效力奠定交易基础，强制披露保障知情权，滥用行为禁止划定营销红线，信息收集规范约束数据利用。企业合规的关键在于：**披露前置且格式合规、同意获取须为明示且留痕、营销行为严守时间与方式限制、信息处理履行保密义务**。

**延伸提醒**：其一，上述规则分散于多个监管机构，企业应建立跨部门合规映射表，避免遗漏；其二，州法层面（如加州消费者隐私法）可能叠加更严格义务，联邦规则仅为底线；其三，法规修订频繁（如§64.611近年多次修正），建议建立法规动态跟踪机制。

64.611 Internet-based TRS registration.

(a)
Default provider registration.
Every provider of VRS or IP Relay must, no later than December 31, 2008, provide users with the capability to register with that VRS or IP Relay provider as a “default provider.” Upon a user's registration, the VRS or IP Relay provider shall:
(1)
Either:
(i)
Facilitate the user's valid number portability request as set forth in
47 CFR 52.34
; or, if the user does not wish to port a number,
(
ii
)
Assign that user a geographically appropriate North American Numbering Plan telephone number; and


(2)
Route and deliver all of that user's inbound and outbound calls unless the user chooses to place a call with, or receives a call from, an alternate provider.
(3)
Certification of eligibility of VRS users.
(i)
A VRS provider seeking compensation from the TRS Fund for providing VRS to a particular user registered with that provider must first obtain a written certification from the user, attesting that the user is eligible to use VRS.
(
ii
)
The certification required by
paragraph (a)(3)(i)
of this section must include the user's attestation that:
(A)
The user has a hearing or speech disability; and

(B)
The user understands that the cost of VRS calls is paid for by contributions from other telecommunications users to the TRS Fund.
(
iii
)
The certification required by
paragraph (a)(3)(i)
of this section must be made on a form separate from any other agreement or form, and must include a separate user signature specific to the certification. For the purposes of this rule, an electronic signature, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, as an electronic sound, symbol, or process, attached to or logically associated with a contract or other record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record, has the same legal effect as a written signature.

 For the purposes of this rule, an electronic record, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act as a contract or other record created, generated, sent, communicated, received, or stored by electronic means, constitutes a record.
(
iv
)
Each VRS provider shall maintain the confidentiality of any registration and certification information obtained by the provider, and may not disclose such registration and certification information or the content of such registration and certification information except as required by law or regulation.

(v)
VRS providers must, for existing registered Internet-based TRS users, submit the certification required by
paragraph (a)(3)(i)
of this section to the TRS User Registration Database within 60 days of notice from the Managing Director that the TRS User Registration Database is ready to accept such information.
(
vi
)
When registering a user that is transferring service from another VRS provider, VRS providers shall obtain and submit a properly executed certification if a query of the TRS User Registration Database shows a properly executed certification has not been filed.
(
vii
)


VRS providers shall require their CAs to terminate any call which does not involve an individual eligible to use VRS due to a hearing or speech disability or, pursuant to the provider's policies, the call does not appear to be a legitimate VRS call, and VRS providers may not seek compensation for such calls from the TRS Fund.

(4)
TRS User Registration Database Information Requirements for VRS.
Each VRS provider shall collect and transmit to the TRS User Registration Database, in a format prescribed by the administrator of the TRS User Registration Database, the following information for each of its new and existing registered internet-based TRS users: Full name; address; ten-digit telephone number assigned in the TRS numbering directory; last four digits of the social security number or Tribal Identification number, if the registered internet-based TRS user is a member of a Tribal nation and does not have a social security number; date of birth; Registered Location; VRS provider name and dates of service initiation and termination;

 a digital copy of the user's self-certification of eligibility for VRS and the date obtained by the provider; the date on which the user's identification was verified; and (for existing users only) the date on which the registered internet-based TRS user last placed a point-to-point or relay call.

(i)
Each VRS provider must obtain, from each new and existing registered internet-based TRS user, consent to transmit the registered internet-based TRS user's information to the TRS User Registration Database. Prior to obtaining consent, the VRS provider must describe to the registered internet-based TRS user, using clear, easily understood language, the specific information being transmitted, that the information is being transmitted to the TRS User Registration Database to ensure proper administration of the TRS program, and that failure to provide consent will result in the registered internet-based TRS user being denied service. VRS providers must obtain and keep a record of affirmative acknowledgment by every registered internet-based TRS user of such consent.
(
ii
)


VRS providers must, for existing registered internet-based TRS users, submit the information in
paragraph (a)(3)
of this section to the TRS User Registration Database within 60 days of notice from the Commission that the TRS User Registration Database is ready to accept such information. Calls from or to existing registered internet-based TRS users that have not had their information populated in the TRS User Registration Database within 60 days of notice from the Commission that the TRS User Registration Database is ready to accept such information shall not be compensable.
(
iii
)


VRS providers must submit the information in the introductory text of
paragraph (a)(4)
of this section upon initiation of service for users registered after 60 days of notice from the Commission that the TRS User Registration Database is ready to accept such information. VRS providers may provide service to such users for up to two weeks after the user's registration information has been submitted to the TRS User Registration Database pending verification of the user's identity.

 After the user's identity is verified by the Database administrator, VRS providers may seek TRS Fund compensation for calls handled during such pre-verification period of up to two weeks.
(
iv
)
If a VRS user's registration data submitted pursuant to
paragraph (a)(4)(iii)


of this section is not verified by the TRS User Registration Database administrator within two weeks after submission, the VRS provider shall hold the assigned number for up to 30 days or the pendency of an appeal, whichever is later, pending the outcome of any further efforts to complete verification, before returning the number to inactive status or assigning it to another user. If a VRS user's identity is verified within such 30-day period, or during the pendency of an appeal, whichever is later, the administrator may enter the number into the Database (and the TRS Numbering Directory) as assigned to that user.

(5)
Assignment of iTRS Numbers to Hearing Point-to-Point Video Users.
(i)
Before assigning an iTRS telephone number to a hearing individual, a VRS provider shall obtain from such individual, the individual's full name, residential address, date of birth, and a written certification, attesting that the individual:
(A)
Is proficient in sign language;
(B)
Understands that the iTRS number may be used only for the purpose of point-to-point communication over distances with registered VRS users; and

(C)
Understands that such iTRS number may not be used to access VRS.
(
ii
)
Before assigning an iTRS telephone number to a hearing individual, a VRS provider also shall obtain the individual's consent to provide the information required by this
paragraph (a)(5)
to the TRS User Registration Database. Before obtaining such consent, the VRS provider, using clear, easily understood language, shall describe the specific information to be provided, explain that the information is provided to ensure proper administration of the TRS program and inform the individual that failure to provide consent will result in denial of service. VRS providers shall obtain and keep a record of affirmative acknowledgment of such consent by every hearing point-to-point video user to whom an iTRS number is assigned.


(
iii
)
The certification required by
paragraph (a)(5)(i)
of this section must be made on a form separate from any other agreement or form, and must include a separate signature specific to the certification. For the purposes of this rule, an electronic signature, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, as an electronic sound, symbol, or process, attached to or logically associated with a contract or other record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record, has the same legal effect as a written signature.

 For the purposes of this rule, an electronic record, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act as a contract or other record created, generated, sent, communicated, received, or stored by electronic means, constitutes a record.
(
iv
)
Before commencing service to any hearing point-to-point video user to whom a VRS provider assigns an iTRS number on or after the TRS User Registration Database is operational, a VRS provider shall submit to the TRS User Registration Database the information listed in
paragraph (a)(5)(i)
of this section and the following additional information:

(A)
The ten-digit telephone number assigned in the TRS Numbering Directory to the hearing point-to-point user;
(B)
The VRS provider's name and the date of service initiation; and
(C)
The date on which a ten-digit number was assigned to or removed from a hearing point-to-point user.

(v)
For all other hearing point-to-point video users to whom a VRS provider has assigned an iTRS number, the VRS provider shall transmit the information required by
paragraph (a)(5)(iv)
of this section within 60 days after the TRS User Registration Database is operational.
(
vi
)
Upon the termination of service to any hearing point-to-point video user, a VRS provider shall submit to the TRS User Registration Database the date of termination of service.
(
vii
)
A VRS provider shall maintain the confidentiality of the information about hearing individuals required by this
paragraph (a)(5)
and may not disclose such information except as required by law or regulation.
(
viii
)


Before commencing service to a hearing point-to-point video user who is transferring point-to-point video service from another VRS provider, a VRS provider shall notify the TRS User Registration Database of such transfer and shall obtain and submit a properly executed certification under
paragraph (a)(5)(i)
of this section.
(
ix
)
Hearing individuals who are assigned iTRS numbers under this
paragraph (a)(5)
shall not be deemed registered VRS users. VRS providers shall not be compensated and shall not seek compensation from the TRS Fund for any VRS calls to or from such iTRS numbers.

(6)
Enterprise and public videophones
—(i)
Definition.
For purposes of this section, a default VRS provider for an enterprise or public videophone is the VRS provider that assigns a North American Numbering Plan (NANP) telephone number to such videophone or receives a port of such number.
(
ii
)
Enterprise and public videophone certification.


(A)
Written certification.
A default VRS provider for an enterprise or public videophone shall obtain a written certification from the individual responsible for the videophone, attesting that the individual understands the functions of the videophone and that the cost of VRS calls made on the videophone is financed by the federally regulated Interstate TRS Fund, and for enterprise videophones, that the organization, business, or agency will make reasonable efforts to ensure that only persons with a hearing or speech disability are permitted to use the phone for VRS.

(B)
Electronic signatures.
The certification required by
paragraph (a)(6)(ii)(A)
of this section must be made on a form separate from any other agreement or form, and must include a separate signature specific to the certification. For the purposes of this
paragraph (a)(6)(ii)(B)
, an electronic signature, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act as an electronic sound, symbol, or process, attached to or logically associated with a contract or other record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record, has the same legal effect as a written signature. For the purposes of this
paragraph (a)(6)(ii)(B)


, an electronic record, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act as a contract or other record created, generated, sent, communicated, received, or stored by electronic means, constitutes a record.

(C)
Consent for transmission and confidentiality of enterprise and public videophone registration.
A default VRS provider for an enterprise or public videophone must obtain consent from the individual responsible for the videophone to transmit the information required by this section to the TRS User Registration Database. Before obtaining such consent, a VRS provider must describe to such individual, using clear, easily understood language, the specific information being transmitted, that the information is being transmitted to the TRS User Registration Database to ensure proper administration of the TRS program, and that failure to provide consent will result in denial of service to the videophone.

 A VRS provider must obtain and keep a record of affirmative acknowledgment of such consent for every enterprise and public videophone. A VRS provider shall maintain the confidentiality of any registration and certification information obtained by the provider, and may not disclose such registration and certification information, or the content of such registration and certification information, except as required by law or regulation.
(
iii
)
Enterprise and public videophone registration.


A default VRS provider for an enterprise or public videophone shall transmit to the TRS User Registration Database, in a format prescribed by the administrator of the TRS User Registration Database, the following information for each enterprise or public videophone for which it assigns (or receives a port of) a North American Numbering Plan telephone number or for which it is the default VRS provider:

(A)
The default VRS provider's name;
(B)
The NANP telephone number assigned to the videophone;
(C)
The name and physical address of the organization, business, or agency where the enterprise or public videophone is located, and the Registered Location of the phone if that is different from the physical address;
(D)
Whether the videophone is a public or enterprise videophone, and for enterprise videophones, the type of location where the videophone is located within the organization, business, agency, or other entity, such as, but not limited to, a reception desk or other work area, a private workspace, a private room in a long-term care facility, or another restricted area;
(E)
The date of initiation of service to the videophone by the default VRS provider;


(F)
The name of the individual responsible for the videophone, confirmation that the provider has obtained the certification required by
paragraph (a)(6)(ii)
of this section, and the date the certification was obtained by the provider; and

(G)
Whether the device is assigned to a hearing individual who knows sign language.
(
iv
)
Transmission of data to the TRS User Registration Database.
Default VRS providers shall transmit the information required by
paragraph (a)(6)(iii)
of this section for existing enterprise and public videophones within 120 days after notice from the Commission that the TRS User Registration Database is ready to accept such information. For videophones placed in service more than 120 days after such notice, the default VRS provider shall submit the required information and certification before initiating service.

 VRS calls placed to or from enterprise or public videophones more than 120 days after such notice shall not be compensable if the required registration information was not received by the TRS User Registration Database before placement of the call.

(v)
Notice of removal or disconnection of enterprise and public videophones.
VRS providers shall notify the TRS Fund administrator within one business day in the event that a registered enterprise or public videophone is removed or permanently disconnected from VRS.
(b)
Mandatory registration of new users.
As of December 31, 2008, VRS and IP Relay providers must, prior to the initiation of service for an individual that has not previously utilized VRS or IP Relay, register that new user as described in
paragraph (a)
of this section.
(c)
Obligations of default providers and former default providers.
(1)
Default providers must:


(i)
Obtain current routing information from their Registered internet-based TRS Users, registered enterprise and public videophones, and hearing point-to-point video users;
(
ii
)
Provision such information to the TRS Numbering Directory; and
(
iii
)
Maintain such information in their internal databases and in the TRS Numbering Directory.
(2)
Internet-based TRS providers (and, to the extent necessary, their Numbering Partners) must:


(i)
Take such steps as are necessary to cease acquiring routing information from any VRS, IP Relay, or hearing point-to-point video user, or any individual responsible for maintaining an enterprise or public videophone, that ports a NANP telephone number to another VRS or IP Relay provider or otherwise selects a new default provider; and
(
ii
)
Communicate among themselves as necessary to ensure that:
(A)
Only the default provider provisions routing information to the central database; and


(B)
VRS and IP Relay providers other than the default provider are aware that they must query the TRS Numbering Directory in order to obtain accurate routing information for a particular user of VRS or IP Relay, or for an enterprise or public videophone.
(d)
Proxy numbers.
After December 31, 2008, a VRS or IP Relay provider:
(1)
May not assign or issue a proxy or alias for a NANP telephone number to any user; and
(2)
Must cease to use any proxy or alias for a NANP telephone number assigned or issued to any Registered Internet-based TRS User.
(e)
Toll free numbers.
A VRS or IP Relay provider:


(1)
May not assign or issue a toll free number to any VRS or IP Relay user.
(2)
That has already assigned or provided a toll free number to a VRS or IP Relay user must, at the VRS or IP Relay user's request, facilitate the transfer of the toll free number to a toll free subscription with a toll free service provider that is under the direct control of the user.
(3)
Must within one year after the effective date of this Order remove from the Internet-based TRS Numbering Directory any toll free number that has not been transferred to a subscription with a toll free service provider and for which the user is the subscriber of record.


(f)
iTRS access technology.
(1)
Every VRS or IP Relay provider must ensure that all iTRS access technology they have issued, leased, or otherwise provided to VRS or IP Relay users delivers routing information or other information only to the user's default provider, except as is necessary to complete or receive “dial around” calls on a case-by-case basis.
(2)
All iTRS access technology issued, leased, or otherwise provided to VRS or IP Relay users by Internet-based TRS providers must be capable of facilitating the requirements of this section.


(g)
User notification.
Every VRS or IP Relay provider must include an advisory on its website and in any promotional materials addressing numbering or E911 services for VRS or IP Relay.
(1)
At a minimum, the advisory must address the following issues:

(i)
The process by which VRS or IP Relay users may obtain ten-digit telephone numbers, including a brief summary of the numbering assignment and administration processes adopted herein;
(
ii
)
The portability of ten-digit telephone numbers assigned to VRS or IP Relay users;
(
iii
)
The process by which persons using VRS or IP Relay may submit, update, and confirm receipt by the provider of their Registered Location information;
(
iv
)
An explanation emphasizing the importance of maintaining accurate, up-to-date Registered Location information with the user's default provider in the event that the individual places an emergency call via an Internet-based relay service;


(v)
The process by which a VRS or IP Relay user may acquire a toll free number, or transfer control of a toll free number from a VRS or IP Relay provider to the user;
(
vi
)
The process by which persons holding a toll free number request that the toll free number be linked to their ten-digit telephone number in the TRS Numbering Directory; and
(
vii
)
If the provider assigns iTRS numbers to hearing point-to-point video users, an explanation that hearing point-to-point video users will not be able to place an emergency call.


(2)
VRS and IP Relay providers must obtain and keep a record of affirmative acknowledgment by every Registered Internet-based TRS User of having received and understood the advisory described in this subsection.

IP CTS Registration and Certification Requirements
.(i)
IP CTS providers must first obtain the following registration information from each consumer prior to requesting compensation from the TRS Fund for service provided to the consumer: The consumer's full name, date of birth, last four digits of the consumer's social security number, full residential address, and telephone number.

vi

(A)
Be qualified to evaluate an individual's hearing loss in accordance with applicable professional standards, and must be either a physician, audiologist, or other hearing related professional. Such professional shall not have been referred to the IP CTS user, either directly or indirectly, by any provider of TRS or any officer, director, partner, employee, agent, subcontractor, or sponsoring organization or entity (collectively “affiliate”) of any TRS provider. Nor shall the third party professional making such certification have any business, family or social relationship with the TRS provider or any affiliate of the TRS provider from which the consumer is receiving or will receive service.


(B)
Provide his or her name, title, and contact information, including address, telephone number, and email address.

(C)
Certify in writing, under penalty of perjury, that the IP CTS user is an individual with hearing loss that necessitates use of captioned telephone service and that the third party professional understands that the captioning on captioned telephone service is provided by a live communications assistant and is funded through a federal program.
(
xi
)
In instances where the consumer has obtained IP CTS equipment from a local, state, or federal governmental program, the consumer may present documentation to the IP CTS provider demonstrating that the equipment was obtained through one of these programs, in lieu of providing an independent, third-party certification under
paragraphs (j)(1)(vii)
and


(ix)
of this section.
(
xii
)
Each IP CTS provider shall maintain records of any registration and certification information for a period of at least five years after the consumer ceases to obtain service from the provider and shall maintain the confidentiality of such registration and certification information, and may not disclose such registration and certification information or the content of such registration and certification information except as required by law or regulation.
(
xiii
)
[Reserved]
(2)
TRS User Registration Database Information for IP CTS.


(i)
Each IP CTS Provider shall collect and transmit to the TRS User Registration Database, in a format prescribed by the administrator of the TRS User Registration Database, the following information for each of its new and existing registered IP CTS users:
(A)
Full name;
(B)
Full residential address;
(C)
Telephone number;
(D)
A unique identifier such as the electronic serial number (ESN) of the user's IP CTS device, the user's log-in identification, or the user's email address;


(E)
The last four digits of the user's social security number or Tribal Identification number (or alternative documentation, if such documentation is permitted by and has been collected pursuant to
Misuse of internet Protocol (IP) Captioned Telephone Service; Telecommunications Relay Services and Speech-to-Speech Services for Individuals with Hearing and Speech Disabilities,
Order, 30 FCC Rcd 1093 (CGB 2015));
(F)
Date of birth;
(G)
Registered Location (if applicable);
(H)
IP CTS provider name;
(I)
Date of service initiation and (when applicable) termination;


(J)
A digital copy of the user's self-certification of eligibility for IP CTS and the date obtained by the provider; and

(K)
For existing users onlythe date on which the IP CTS user last placed an IP CTS call.
(
ii
)
Each IP CTS provider shall obtain, from each new and existing registered IP CTS user, consent to transmit the registered IP CTS user's information to the TRS User Registration Database. Prior to obtaining such consent, the IP CTS provider shall describe to the registered IP CTS user, using clear, easily understood language, the specific information obtained by the IP CTS provider from the user that is to be transmitted, and inform the user that the information is being transmitted to the TRS User Registration Database to ensure proper administration of the TRS program, and that failure to provide consent will result in the registered IP CTS user being denied service.

 IP CTS providers shall keep a record of affirmative acknowledgment of such consent by every registered IP CTS user.
(
iii
)
Registration of Emergency Shelter Devices.
An IP CTS provider may seek and receive TRS Fund compensation for the provision of captioning service to users of a temporary, public IP CTS device set up in an emergency shelter, provided that, before commencing service to such a device, the IP CTS provider collects, maintains in its registration records, and submits to the TRS User Registration Database all information reasonably requested by the administrator, including the telephone number and location of the device.

 IP CTS providers shall remove the device's registration information from the Database when service for such a device is terminated.
(
iv
)
By the date of initiation of service to an IP CTS user or device, or one year after notice from the Commission that the TRS User Registration Database is ready to accept such information, whichever is later, IP CTS providers shall submit to the TRS User Registration Database the registration information required by
paragraph (j)(2)(i)
or

(iii)
of this section. Calls from or to registered IP CTS users or devices whose registration information has not been populated in the TRS User Registration Database by the applicable date shall not be compensable, and an IP CTS provider shall not seek TRS Fund compensation for such calls.

(v)
IP CTS providers may provide service to new users for up to two weeks after the user's registration information has been submitted to the TRS User Registration Database pending verification of the user's identity. After a user's identity is verified by the Database administrator, IP CTS providers may seek TRS Fund compensation for calls handled during such pre-verification period.
(
vi
)
When registering a user who is transferring service from another IP CTS provider, IP CTS providers shall obtain and submit a digital copy of a user's self-certification of eligibility if a query of the TRS User Registration Database shows a properly executed certification has not been filed.


(3)
An IP CTS provider shall not seek TRS Fund compensation for providing captioning service to any individual or device if the registration information for such individual or device has been removed from the TRS User Registration Database, or if the provider obtains information that the individual or device is
not eligible to receive IP CTS.


(k)
Individual registration for use of TRS in correctional facilities
—(1)
Registration information and documentation.
If an individual eligible to use TRS registers with an internet-based TRS provider while incarcerated, the provider shall collect and transmit to the TRS User Registration Database the information and documentation required by the applicable provisions of this section, except that:


(i)
The residential address specified for such Incarcerated Person shall be the name of the correctional authority with custody of that person along with the main or administrative address of such authority;
(
ii
)
A Registered Location need not be provided; and
(
iii
)
If an Incarcerated Person has no Social Security number or Tribal Identification number, an identification number assigned by the correctional authority along with the facility identification number, if there is one, may be provided in lieu of the last four digits of a Social Security number or a Tribal Identification number.


(2)
Verification of VRS and IP CTS registration data.
An Incarcerated Person's identity and address may be verified pursuant to
§ 64.615(a)(6) of this chapter
, for purposes of VRS or IP CTS registration, based on documentation, such as a letter or statement, provided by an official of a correctional authority that states the name of the person; the person's identification number assigned by the correctional authority; the name of the correctional authority; and the address of the correctional facility. The VRS or IP CTS provider shall transmit such documentation to the TRS User Registration Database administrator.

(3)
Release or transfer of an Incarcerated Person.
Upon release (or transfer to a different correction authority) of an Incarcerated Person who has registered for VRS or IP CTS, the VRS or IP CTS provider with which such person has registered shall update the person's registration information within 30 days of receiving written notification from such person or the correctional authority of such release or transfer. Such updated information shall include, in the case of release, the individual's full residential address, Registered Location (if required by this section or
part 9 of this chapter
), and any other registration information required by this section and not previously provided, and in the case of transfer shall include the information required by
paragraph (k)(2)
of this section.


(4)
Dial-around calls for VRS.
VRS providers shall not allow dial-around calls by Incarcerated People.
(l)
Enterprise registration for the use of TRS in correctional facilities.
(1)
Notwithstanding the other provisions of this section, a TRS provider may provide VRS, IP Relay, or IP CTS to an Incarcerated Person, without individual user registration, if the TRS provider has completed enterprise registration of the correctional facility or correctional authority for which service will be provided.
(2)
[Reserved]
(3)
[Reserved]

(4)
Confidentiality.
The TRS provider shall maintain the confidentiality of any registration and certification information obtained by the TRS provider, and shall not disclose such registration and certification information, or the content of such registration and certification information, except as required by law or regulation.

54.419 Validity of electronic signatures.
(a)
For the purposes of this , an electronic signature, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, as an electronic sound, symbol, or process, attached to or logically associated with a contract or other record and executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record, has the same legal effect as a written signature.
(b)
For the purposes of this , an electronic record, defined by the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act as a contract or other record created, generated, sent, communicated, received, or stored by electronic means, constitutes a record.

1005.18 Requirements for financial institutions offering prepaid accounts.
(a)
Coverage.
A financial institution shall comply with all applicable requirements of the Act and this part with respect to prepaid accounts except as modified by this section. For rules governing government benefit accounts, see
§ 1005.15
.(b)
Pre-acquisition disclosure requirements
—(1)
Timing of disclosures
—(i)
General.
Except as provided in
paragraph (b)(1)(ii)
or

(iii)
of this section, a financial institution shall provide the disclosures required by
paragraph (b)
of this section before a consumer acquires a prepaid account. When a prepaid account is used for disbursing funds to a consumer, and the financial institution or third party making the disbursement does not offer any alternative means for the consumer to receive those funds in lieu of accepting the prepaid account, for purposes of this paragraph, the disclosures required by
paragraph (b)
of this section may be provided at the time the consumer receives the prepaid account.
(
ii
)
Disclosures for prepaid accounts acquired in retail locations.
A financial institution is not required to provide the long form disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(4)


of this section before a consumer acquires a prepaid account in person at a retail location if the following conditions are met:

(A)
The prepaid account access device is contained inside the packaging material.
(B)
The disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(2)
of this section is provided on or are visible through an outward-facing, external surface of a prepaid account access device's packaging material.
(C)
The disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(2)
of this section includes the information set forth in
paragraph (b)(2)(xiii)
of this section that allows a consumer to access the information required to be disclosed by
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section by telephone and via a website.

(D)
The long form disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section is provided after the consumer acquires the prepaid account. If a financial institution does not provide the long form disclosure inside the prepaid account packaging material, and it is not otherwise already mailing or delivering to the consumer written account-related communications within 30 days of obtaining the consumer's contact information, it may provide the long form disclosure pursuant to this paragraph in electronic form without regard to the consumer notice and consent requirements of section 101(c) of the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (E-Sign Act) (
15 U.S.C. 7001
et seq.
).
(
iii
)
Disclosures for prepaid accounts acquired orally by telephone.


A financial institution is not required to provide the long form disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section before a consumer acquires a prepaid account orally by telephone if the following conditions are met:

(A)
The financial institution communicates to the consumer orally, before the consumer acquires the prepaid account, that the information required to be disclosed by
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section is available both by telephone and on a Web site.
(B)
The financial institution makes the information required to be disclosed by
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section available both by telephone and on a Web site.
(C)
The long form disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section is provided after the consumer acquires the prepaid account.
(2)
Short form disclosure content.
In accordance with
paragraph (b)(1)
of this section, a financial institution shall provide a disclosure setting forth the following fees and information for a prepaid account, as applicable:

(i)
Periodic fee.
The periodic fee charged for holding the prepaid account, assessed on a monthly or other periodic basis, using the term “Monthly fee,” “Annual fee,” or a substantially similar term.
(
ii
)
Per purchase fee.
The fee for making a purchase using the prepaid account, using the term “Per purchase” or a substantially similar term.
(
iii
)
ATM withdrawal fees.
Two fees for using an automated teller machine to initiate a withdrawal of cash in the United States from the prepaid account, both within and outside of the financial institution's network or a network affiliated with the financial institution, using the term “ATM withdrawal” or a substantially similar term, and “in-network” or “out-of-network,” respectively, or substantially similar terms.
(
iv
)
Cash reload fee.


The fee for reloading cash into the prepaid account using the term “Cash reload” or a substantially similar term. The fee disclosed must be the total of all charges from the financial institution and any third parties for a cash reload.

(v)
ATM balance inquiry fees.
Two fees for using an automated teller machine to check the balance of the prepaid account in the United States, both within and outside of the financial institution's network or a network affiliated with the financial institution, using the term “ATM balance inquiry” or a substantially similar term, and “in-network” or “out-of-network,” respectively, or substantially similar terms.
(
vi
)
Customer service fees.


Two fees for calling the financial institution about the prepaid account, both for calling an interactive voice response system and a live customer service agent, using the term “Customer service” or a substantially similar term, and “automated” or “live agent,” or substantially similar terms, respectively, and “per call” or a substantially similar term. When providing a short form disclosure for multiple service plans pursuant to
paragraph (b)(6)(iii)(B)(

2)
of this section, disclose only the fee for calling the live agent customer service about the prepaid account, using the term “Live customer service” or a substantially similar term and “per call” or a substantially similar term.
(
vii
)
Inactivity fee.
The fee for non-use, dormancy, or inactivity of the prepaid account, using the term “Inactivity” or a substantially similar term, as well as the conditions that trigger the financial institution to impose that fee.
(
viii
)
Statements regarding additional fee types
—(A)
Statement regarding number of additional fee types charged.


A statement disclosing the number of additional fee types the financial institution may charge consumers with respect to the prepaid account, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “We charge [x] other types of fees.” The number of additional fee types disclosed must reflect the total number of fee types under which the financial institution may charge fees, excluding:

(1)
Fees required to be disclosed pursuant to
paragraphs (b)(2)(i)
through
(vii)
and
(b)(5)
of this section; and

(2)
Any finance charges as described in Regulation Z,
12 CFR 1026.4(b)(11)
, imposed in connection with a covered separate credit feature accessible by a hybrid prepaid-credit card as defined in
12 CFR 1026.61
.(B)
Statement directing consumers to disclosure of additional fee types.
If a financial institution makes a disclosure pursuant to
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)
of this section, a statement directing consumers to that disclosure, located after but on the same line of text as the statement regarding the number of additional fee types required by
paragraph (b)(2)(viii)(A)
of this section, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Here are some of them:”.
(
ix
)
Disclosure of additional fee types
—(A)
Determination of which additional fee types to disclose.


The two fee types that generate the highest revenue from consumers for the prepaid account program or across prepaid account programs that share the same fee schedule during the time period provided in
paragraphs (b)(2)(ix)(D)
and

(E)
of this section, excluding:
(1)
Fees required to be disclosed pursuant to
paragraphs (b)(2)(i)
through
(vii)
and
(b)(5)
of this section;
(2)
Any fee types that generated less than 5 percent of the total revenue from consumers for the prepaid account program or across prepaid account programs that share the same fee schedule during the time period provided in
paragraphs (b)(2)(ix)(D)
and
(E)
of this section; and

(3)
Any finance charges as described in Regulation Z,
12 CFR 1026.4(b)(11)
, imposed in connection with a covered separate credit feature accessible by a hybrid prepaid-credit card as defined in
12 CFR 1026.61
.(B)
Disclosure of fewer than two additional fee types.
A financial institution that has only one additional fee type that satisfies the criteria in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(A)
of this section must disclose that one additional fee type; it may, but is not required to, also disclose another additional fee type of its choice. A financial institution that has no additional fee types that satisfy the criteria in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(A)
of this section is not required to make a disclosure under this
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)
;

 it may, but is not required to, disclose one or two fee types of its choice.

(C)
Fee variations in additional fee types.
If an additional fee type required to be disclosed pursuant to
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(A)
of this section has more than two fee variations, or when providing a short form disclosure for multiple service plans pursuant to
paragraph (b)(6)(iii)(B)(
2)
of this section, the financial institution must disclose the name of the additional fee type and the highest fee amount in accordance with
paragraph (b)(3)(i)
of this section; for disclosures other than for multiple service plans, it may, but is not required to, consolidate the fee variations into two categories and disclose the names of those two fee variation categories and the fee amounts in a format substantially similar to that used to disclose the two-tier fees required by
paragraphs (b)(2)(v)
and


(vi)
of this section and in accordance with
paragraphs (b)(3)(i)
and
(b)(7)(ii)(B)(
1)
of this section. Except when providing a short form disclosure for multiple service plans pursuant to
paragraph (b)(6)(iii)(B)(
2)
of this section, if an additional fee type has two fee variations, the financial institution must disclose the name of the additional fee type together with the names of the two fee variations and the fee amounts in a format substantially similar to that used to disclose the two-tier fees required by
paragraphs (b)(2)(v)
and
(vi)
of this section and in accordance with
paragraph (b)(7)(ii)(B)(


1)
of this section. If a financial institution only charges one fee under a particular fee type, the financial institution must disclose the name of the additional fee type and the fee amount; it may, but is not required to, disclose also the name of the one fee variation for which the fee amount is charged, in a format substantially similar to that used to disclose the two-tier fees required by
paragraphs (b)(2)(v)
and
(vi)
of this section, except that the financial institution would disclose only the one fee variation name and fee amount instead of two.


(D)
Timing of initial assessment of additional fee types disclosure
—(1)
Existing prepaid account programs as of April 1, 2019.
For a prepaid account program in effect as of April 1, 2019, the financial institution must disclose the additional fee types based on revenue for a 24-month period that begins no earlier than October 1, 2014.


(2)
Existing prepaid account programs as of April 1, 2019 with unavailable data.
If a financial institution does not have 24 months of fee revenue data for a particular prepaid account program from which to calculate the additional fee types disclosure in advance of April 1, 2019, the financial institution must disclose the additional fee types based on revenue it reasonably anticipates the prepaid account program will generate over the 24-month period that begins on April 1, 2019.


(3)
New prepaid account programs created on or after April 1, 2019.
For a prepaid account program created on or after April 1, 2019, the financial institution must disclose the additional fee types based on revenue it reasonably anticipates the prepaid account program will generate over the first 24 months of the program.
(E)
Timing of periodic reassessment and update of additional fee types disclosure
—(1)
General.
A financial institution must reassess its additional fee types disclosure periodically as described in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)(
2)
of this section and upon a fee schedule change as described in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)(

3)
of this section. The financial institution must update its additional fee types disclosure if the previous disclosure no longer complies with the requirements of this
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)
.(2)
Periodic reassessment.
A financial institution must reassess whether its previously disclosed additional fee types continue to comply with the requirements of this
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)
every 24 months based on revenue for the previous 24-month period. The financial institution must complete this reassessment and update its disclosure, if applicable, within three months of the end of the 24-month period, except as provided in the update printing exception in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)(


4)
of this section. A financial institution may, but is not required to, carry out this reassessment and update, if applicable, more frequently than every 24 months, at which time a new 24-month period commences.

(3)
Fee schedule change.
If a financial institution revises the fee schedule for a prepaid account program, it must determine whether it reasonably anticipates that the previously disclosed additional fee types will continue to comply with the requirements of this
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)
for the 24 months following implementation of the fee schedule change. If the financial institution reasonably anticipates that the previously disclosed additional fee types will not comply with the requirements of this
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)
, it must update the disclosure based on its reasonable anticipation of what those additional fee types will be at the time the fee schedule change goes into effect, except as provided in the update printing exception in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)(


4)
of this section. If an immediate change in terms and conditions is necessary to maintain or restore the security of an account or an electronic fund transfer system as described in
§ 1005.8(a)(2)
and that change affects the prepaid account program's fee schedule, the financial institution must complete its reassessment and update its disclosure, if applicable, within three months of the date it makes the change permanent, except as provided in the update printing exception in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)(
4)
of this section.


(4)
Update printing exception.
Notwithstanding the requirements to update an additional fee types disclosure in
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)
of this section, a financial institution is not required to update the listing of additional fee types that are provided on, in, or with prepaid account packaging materials that were manufactured, printed, or otherwise produced prior to a periodic reassessment and update pursuant to
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)(
2)
of this section or prior to a fee schedule change pursuant to
paragraph (b)(2)(ix)(E)(
3)
of this section.

(x)
Statement regarding overdraft credit features.
If a covered separate credit feature accessible by a hybrid prepaid-credit card as defined in Regulation Z,
12 CFR 1026.61
, may be offered at any point to a consumer in connection with the prepaid account, a statement that overdraft/credit may be offered, the time period after which it may be offered, and that fees would apply, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “You may be offered overdraft/credit after [x] days. Fees would apply.” If no such credit feature will be offered at any point to a consumer in connection with the prepaid account, a statement that no overdraft credit feature is offered, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “No overdraft/credit feature.”
(
xi
)


Statement regarding registration and FDIC or NCUA insurance.
A statement regarding the prepaid account program's eligibility for FDIC deposit insurance or NCUA share insurance, as appropriate, and directing the consumer to register the prepaid account for insurance and other account protections, where applicable, as follows:

(A)
Account is insurance eligible and does not have pre-acquisition consumer identification/verification.
If a prepaid account program is set up to be eligible for FDIC deposit or NCUA share insurance, and consumer identification and verification does not occur before the account is opened, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Register your card for [FDIC insurance eligibility] [NCUA insurance, if eligible,] and other protections.”


(B)
Account is not insurance eligible and does not have pre-acquisition consumer identification/verification.
If a prepaid account program is not set up to be eligible for FDIC deposit or NCUA share insurance, and consumer identification and verification does not occur before the account is opened, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Not [FDIC] [NCUA] insured. Register your card for other protections.”


(C)
Account is insurance eligible and has pre-acquisition consumer identification/verification.
If a prepaid account program is set up to be eligible for FDIC deposit or NCUA share insurance, and consumer identification and verification occurs for all prepaid accounts within the prepaid program before the account is opened, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Your funds are [eligible for FDIC insurance] [NCUA insured, if eligible].”


(D)
Account is not insurance eligible and has pre-acquisition consumer identification/verification.
If a prepaid account program is not set up to be eligible for FDIC deposit or NCUA share insurance, and consumer identification and verification occurs for all prepaid accounts within the prepaid account program before the account is opened, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Your funds are not [FDIC] [NCUA] insured.”

(E)
No consumer identification/verification.
If a prepaid account program is set up such that there is no consumer identification and verification process for any prepaid accounts within the prepaid account program, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Treat this card like cash. Not [FDIC] [NCUA] insured.”
(
xii
)
Statement regarding CFPB Web site.
A statement directing the consumer to a Web site URL of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (
cfpb.gov/prepaid
) for general information about prepaid accounts, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “For general information about prepaid accounts, visit
cfpb.gov/prepaid
.”
(
xiii
)
Statement regarding information on all fees and services.


A statement directing the consumer to the location of the long form disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section to find details and conditions for all fees and services. For a financial institution offering prepaid accounts at a retail location pursuant to the retail location exception in
paragraph (b)(1)(ii)
of this section, this statement must also include a telephone number and a Web site URL that a consumer may use to directly access, respectively, an oral and an electronic version of the long form disclosure required under
paragraph (b)(4)
of this section.

 The disclosure required by this paragraph must be made using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Find details and conditions for all fees and services in [location]” or, for prepaid accounts offered at retail locations pursuant to
paragraph (b)(1)(ii)
of this section, made using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “Find details and conditions for all fees and services inside the package, or call [telephone number] or visit [Web site].” The Web site URL may not exceed 22 characters and must be meaningfully named.

 A financial institution may, but is not required to, disclose an SMS code at the end of the statement disclosing the telephone number and Web site URL, if the SMS code can be accommodated on the same line of text as the statement required by this paragraph.
(
xiv
)
Additional content for payroll card accounts
—(A)
Statement regarding wage or salary payment options.


For payroll card accounts, a statement that the consumer does not have to accept the payroll card account and directing the consumer to ask about other ways to receive wages or salary from the employer instead of receiving them via the payroll card account using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “You do not have to accept this payroll card. Ask your employer about other ways to receive your wages.

” Alternatively, a financial institution may provide a statement that the consumer has several options to receive wages or salary, followed by a list of the options available to the consumer, and directing the consumer to tell the employer which option the consumer chooses using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “You have several options to receive your wages: [list of options available to the consumer]; or this payroll card. Tell your employer which option you choose.” This statement must be located above the information required by paragraphs (b)(2)(i) through (iv).

(B)
Statement regarding state-required information or other fee discounts and waivers.
For payroll card accounts, a financial institution may, but is not required to, include a statement in one additional line of text directing the consumer to a particular location outside the short form disclosure for information on ways the consumer may access payroll card account funds and balance information for free or for a reduced fee. This statement must be located directly below any statements disclosed pursuant to
paragraphs (b)(3)(i)
and
(ii)
of this section, or, if no such statements are disclosed, above the statement required by
paragraph (b)(2)(x)
of this section.


(3)
Short form disclosure of variable fees and third-party fees and prohibition on disclosure of finance charges
—(i)
General disclosure of variable fees.
If the amount of any fee that is required to be disclosed in the short form disclosure pursuant to
paragraphs (b)(2)(i)
through
(vii)
and

(ix)
of this section could vary, a financial institution shall disclose the highest amount it may impose for that fee, followed by a symbol, such as an asterisk, linked to a statement explaining that the fee could be lower depending on how and where the prepaid account is used, using the following clause or a substantially similar clause: “This fee can be lower depending on how and where this card is used.” Except as provided in
paragraph (b)(3)(ii)
of this section, a financial institution must use the same symbol and statement for all fees that could vary. The linked statement must be located above the statement required by
paragraph (b)(2)(x)
of this section.
(
ii
)
Disclosure of variable periodic fee.
If the amount of the periodic fee disclosed in the short form disclosure pursuant to


paragraph (b)(2)(i)
of this section could vary, as an alternative to the disclosure required by
paragraph (b)(3)(i)
of this section, the financial institution may disclose the highest amount it may impose for the periodic fee, followed by a symbol, such as a dagger, that is different from the symbol the financial institution uses pursuant to
paragraph (b)(3)(i)

ii

(

Nothing in this part should be construed to affect the requirement in the Fair Credit Reporting Act,
15 U.S.C. 1681

Requesting or receiving payment of any fee or consideration from a person for goods or services represented to recover or otherwise assist in the return of money or any other item of value paid for by, or promised to, that person in a previous transaction, until seven (7) business days after such money or other item is delivered to that person. This provision shall not apply to goods or services provided to a person by a licensed attorney;

## 一、核心概括

美国《银行保密法》（BSA）通过31 CFR第X章对各金融机构设定反洗钱合规义务，核心要求包括：建立书面反洗钱计划、指定合规官、持续培训、独立测试及基于风险的客户尽职调查。不同机构（银行、共同基金、保险、贷款金融、贵金属交易商）具体要求存在差异，但均须经高级管理层批准并接受FinCEN检查。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 银行的反洗钱计划要求

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Banks (BSAAML)》31 CFR § 1020.210【来源3】

**深度解读**：该条区分受联邦功能监管机构监管的银行与无联邦功能监管机构的银行（如私营银行、非联邦保险信用合作社）。前者实施并维持符合§§1010.610和1010.620的反洗钱计划即视为满足31 U.S.C. § 5318(h)(1)；后者须建立书面计划，并经董事会或同等治理机构批准。两类银行均须包含五项最低要素：内部控制系统、独立测试、指定合规协调人、人员培训、基于风险的持续客户尽职调查（含理解客户关系性质目的、持续监测可疑交易、维护更新客户信息，客户信息须包括法人客户受益所有人信息）。

**重点提示**：无联邦监管机构的银行额外要求董事会批准及应FinCEN要求提供计划副本。客户尽职调查须覆盖法人客户受益所有人（依§ 1010.230定义），这是2016年CDD规则的核心扩展。

**实务指引**：银行应准备董事会决议或批准记录、合规官任命文件、风险评估报告、培训记录、独立测试报告及客户尽职调查档案。常见误区是将独立测试交由合规官本人执行——测试须由银行人员或外部方进行，但不得由负责日常合规协调的人员主导。

### 2. 共同基金的反洗钱计划要求

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Mutual Funds》31 CFR § 1024.210【来源4】

**深度解读**：自2002年7月24日起，每家共同基金须制定并实施书面反洗钱计划，旨在防止被用于洗钱或恐怖融资，并确保遵守BSA及财政部实施条例。计划须经董事会或受托人书面批准，并可供SEC检查。最低要素包括：合理设计的政策程序与内部控制、独立测试（由基金人员或合格外部方进行）、指定负责实施与监测的人员、持续培训、基于风险的客户尽职调查（含理解客户关系性质目的、持续监测可疑交易、维护更新客户信息含法人受益所有人）。

**重点提示**：共同基金的计划批准须为书面形式，且明确可供SEC（而非仅FinCEN）检查，这与银行、贷款金融公司仅向FinCEN提供副本的要求不同。客户尽职调查要素于2016年新增，须覆盖法人客户受益所有人。

**实务指引**：基金应保存董事会书面批准决议、合规官任命书、培训材料与签到记录、独立测试报告、客户风险画像文档。注意独立测试可由基金人员执行，但须确保测试人员不参与计划日常运作，以保持独立性。

### 3. 保险公司的反洗钱计划要求

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Insurance Companies》31 CFR § 1025.210【来源5】

**深度解读**：保险公司须在2006年5月2日前制定并实施适用于其"覆盖产品"的书面反洗钱计划，经高级管理层批准，并应财政部、FinCEN或其指定人要求提供副本。最低要素包括：基于覆盖产品风险评估的政策程序与内部控制（须将保险代理人和经纪人纳入计划、获取有效反洗钱所需的全部客户相关信息）、指定合规官（负责监测代理人经纪人合规、更新计划、培训）、持续培训（可直接培训或核实已由另一保险公司或合格第三方培训）、独立测试（范围频率与产品风险相称，测试人不得为合规官）。已注册为证券经纪自营商的保险公司，若已依§ 1023.210建立计划并遵守，则视为满足本条。

**重点提示**：保险公司的特殊之处在于须将**保险代理人和保险经纪人**整合进反洗钱计划，合规官须监测其合规情况，独立测试亦须覆盖其合规性。培训可通过"核实第三方已培训"方式满足，但须保留核实记录。

**实务指引**：保险公司应准备覆盖产品清单与风险评估、代理人经纪人名单及培训核实记录、合规官监测日志、独立测试报告（测试人非合规官）。常见误区是仅培训内部员工而忽略代理人和经纪人——法规明确要求将其纳入计划并监测其合规。

### 4. 贷款与金融公司的反洗钱计划要求

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Real Estate》31 CFR § 1029.210【来源1】

**深度解读**：每家贷款或金融公司须制定并实施书面反洗钱计划，合理设计以防止被用于便利洗钱或恐怖融资，计划须经高级管理层批准，并应FinCEN或其指定人要求提供副本。最低要素包括：基于产品服务风险评估的政策程序与内部控制（须将代理人和经纪人整合进计划、获取有效反洗钱所需的全部客户相关信息）、指定合规官（负责有效实施、监测代理人经纪人合规、更新计划、培训）、持续培训（可直接培训或核实合格第三方已培训）、独立测试（范围频率与风险相称，测试人不得为合规官，可由第三方或任何非合规官的高管员工执行）。合规日期为2012年8月13日。

**重点提示**：与保险公司类似，贷款金融公司须将代理人和经纪人纳入计划并监测其合规。独立测试可由公司内部高管或员工执行，但不得为指定的合规官，这为中小型公司提供了灵活性。

**实务指引**：应准备高级管理层批准文件、风险评估、代理人经纪人整合方案、培训记录或第三方培训核实、独立测试报告。注意合规日期已过，新设公司须在开业前建立合规计划。

### 5. 贵金属、宝石或珠宝交易商的反洗钱计划要求

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Casinos and Card Clubs》31 CFR § 1027.210【来源2】

**深度解读**：每家交易商须制定并实施书面反洗钱计划，合理设计以防止通过买卖"覆盖商品"便利洗钱和恐怖融资，经高级管理层批准，应财政部通过FinCEN或其指定人要求提供。风险评估须考虑：产品类型、客户供应商分销渠道地理位置的性質、与非既定客户或非受本规则约束交易商交易的程度、付款或账户对账是否涉及被认定为国际恐怖主义赞助国或非合作司法管辖区的账户。计划须包含识别可能涉及洗钱的交易的政策程序（包括合理询问、拒绝完成或终止交易），并列举异常支付方式、客户不愿提供完整信息、要求不保留正常业务记录、异常交易、不符合行业惯例等警示因素。零售商从非交易商非零售商处采购超过§ 1027.100(b)(2)(i)的5万美元门槛时，合规计划仅需针对该等采购。

**重点提示**：交易商的独立测试可由交易商高管或员工执行，但不得为合规官或参与计划运作的人员。实施日期为2006年1月1日或交易商受本条约束后六个月内（以较晚者为准）。风险评估须特别关注地理管辖区因素。

**实务指引**：交易商应准备风险评估文档（含产品、客户、地理因素分析）、可疑交易识别程序与警示因素清单、拒绝/终止交易记录、培训记录、独立测试报告。常见误区是忽略对"非既定客户"交易的额外审查——法规明确将与非既定客户交易的程度列为风险评估因素。

## 三、总结与建议

美国BSA框架下，各类金融机构的反洗钱合规要求虽在细节上因行业而异，但共享五大支柱：**书面计划经高层批准、指定合规官、持续培训、独立测试、基于风险的客户尽职调查**。银行与共同基金的计划须含法人客户受益所有人信息；保险公司与贷款金融公司须将代理人和经纪人纳入计划并监测其合规；贵金属交易商须特别评估地理管辖区风险。违规可能构成BSA违反，面临FinCEN检查与执法。

**行动指引**：立即对照所属行业条文核查计划五要素是否齐备，重点确认独立测试人员与合规官分离、代理人经纪人已整合、客户尽职调查覆盖受益所有人。

**延伸提醒**：其一，各条合规日期不同（共同基金2002年、保险2006年、贷款金融2012年），新设机构须在受约束前建立计划；其二，独立测试的范围频率须与风险评估相称，建议每年至少一次并留存报告；其三，计划须随风险评估变化、法规更新及FinCEN指引持续修订，合规官应建立年度复审机制。

## 一、核心概括

美国《全球及全国商务电子签名法》（ESIGN Act）确立了一项核心原则：**电子签名与电子记录在满足法定条件时，与书面签名和纸质记录具有同等法律效力**。美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）在《联邦法规汇编》第47编第54部分（Universal Service）的多个条款中明确援引并落实了这一原则，涵盖通用服务基金、生命线项目及应急连接基金等场景。以下结合具体条文展开分析。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 电子签名的法定定义与效力等同原则

**法规出处**：美国联邦法规《47 C.F.R. § 54.1812(a)》《§ 54.419(a)》《§ 54.633(a)》《§ 54.1612(a)》【来源1】【来源2】【来源3】【来源5】

**深度解读**：上述四个条款的(a)款措辞几乎完全一致，均规定：凡符合ESIGN Act定义的电子签名——即"附着于或逻辑上关联于合同或其他记录，由签署人以签署意图执行或采用的电子声音、符号或过程"——**具有与书面签名相同的法律效力**。这一规定的立法意图在于消除电子交易中签名形式的法律不确定性，使电子签名在联邦监管项目（如通用服务基金申请、生命线项目资格认证等）中获得与手写签名同等的法律地位。四个条款分别适用于不同子项目，但核心规则统一，体现了FCC在电子签名问题上的一致立场。

**重点提示**：电子签名效力等同的前提是"以签署意图执行或采用"。若电子符号系系统自动生成、当事人并无签署意图，则不构成有效电子签名。此外，该效力等同原则仅针对联邦目的，各州合同法下电子签名的可执行性仍可能受州法影响。

**实务指引**：企业在向USAC（通用服务管理公司）提交电子表格或合同时，应确保电子签名系统能够记录签署人的身份验证信息和签署时间戳，以证明"签署意图"。建议保留签署过程的审计日志，以备合规审查。常见误区是认为任何点击"同意"按钮均构成电子签名——实际上需结合具体情境判断是否存在签署意图。


### 2. 电子记录的法定地位

**法规出处**：美国联邦法规《47 C.F.R. § 54.1812(b)》《§ 54.419(b)》《§ 54.633(b)》《§ 54.1612(b)》【来源1】【来源2】【来源3】【来源5】

**深度解读**：各条款的(b)款一致规定：凡符合ESIGN Act定义的电子记录——即"通过电子方式创建、生成、发送、通信、接收或存储的合同或其他记录"——**构成法律意义上的"记录"** 。这意味着在FCC监管项目中，电子形式保存的文件（如电子申请表、电子账单、电子认证材料）与纸质文件具有同等记录地位。该规定与(a)款形成完整闭环：电子签名解决"签署"的形式问题，电子记录解决"载体"的形式问题，两者共同确保电子交易在联邦监管框架下的完整法律效力。

**重点提示**：电子记录"构成记录"不等于自动满足所有证据法或保存期限要求。FCC各项目可能对记录保存格式、保存期限有单独规定，电子记录仍需符合这些具体要求。

**实务指引**：建议企业建立电子记录管理系统，确保电子记录的完整性、可追溯性和防篡改能力。在向USAC提交材料时，优先采用PDF/A等长期保存格式，并保留元数据（创建时间、修改记录等）。常见误区是将"电子记录有效"误解为"任何电子格式均可"——实际上应确保记录可读、可检索、可复制。


### 3. 多条款并行适用的体系化解读

**法规出处**：《47 C.F.R. § 54.1812》《§ 54.419》《§ 54.633》《§ 54.1612》【来源1】【来源2】【来源3】【来源5】

**深度解读**：四个条款分别位于FCC通用服务基金的不同子部分：§ 54.419适用于通用服务基金的管理条款，§ 54.633适用于生命线/低收入项目，§ 54.1612适用于应急连接基金（Emergency Connectivity Fund），§ 54.1812适用于其他通用服务机制。这种"分散立法、统一规则"的模式表明：FCC有意将电子签名效力规则嵌入每一个具体项目管理框架中，而非仅在总则中作统一规定。其实务意义在于，参与不同FCC项目的实体均可依据对应条款主张电子签名的效力，无需跨条款援引。§ 54.419条后标注的"77 FR 12974, Mar. 2, 2012"显示该条款于2012年经联邦公报正式修订，反映了FCC在电子交易实践发展后的规则更新。

**重点提示**：虽然四个条款内容实质相同，但在具体争议中应援引与所涉项目直接对应的条款，以增强论证的针对性。§ 54.1612条特别标注"Q—Emergency Connectivity Fund"，表明其适用范围限于应急连接基金项目。

**实务指引**：合规人员在准备电子签署文件时，应先确认所涉项目对应的具体条款编号，并在内部合规文件中准确记录法律依据。建议建立条款对照表，将各FCC子项目与对应的电子签名条款一一映射，避免援引错误。


### 4. 与《电话营销销售规则》中电子签名规则的区分适用

**法规出处**：美国联邦法规《16 C.F.R. § 310.4(b)(1)(iii)(B)(1)》及脚注1、2【来源4】

**深度解读**：《电话营销销售规则》（TSR）第310.4条在规范电话营销行为时，也涉及电子签名的使用。该条脚注明确："本部分中'签名'一词包括电子或数字形式的签名，但以该形式签名根据可适用的联邦法或州合同法被认定为有效签名为限。"【来源4】这一规定与ESIGN Act的效力原则相衔接，但适用场景不同：TSR中的电子签名主要用于证明消费者以书面形式同意接收电话营销电话，或授权预录语音电话。值得注意的是，TSR对电子签名的认可附带了"根据可适用的联邦法或州合同法被认定为有效"这一限定条件，比FCC通用服务条款中的表述更为审慎，实质上将效力认定的最终判断权部分让渡给了州合同法。

**重点提示**：在电话营销合规场景中，仅依赖电子签名本身不足以证明同意的有效性，还需确保该电子签名形式在相关州法下被认可。此外，TSR要求书面协议须"清晰证明"消费者授权，并包含电话号码和签名，电子签名须满足这些实质要件。

**实务指引**：电话营销企业如需以电子方式获取消费者书面同意，应：(1)确认目标州是否采纳UETA（统一电子交易法）或类似立法；(2)确保电子同意流程包含清晰的披露声明、消费者主动勾选或签署步骤、以及电话号码的明确记录；(3)保存完整的电子同意记录至少与TSR记录保存期限一致。常见误区是认为ESIGN Act的联邦效力可直接覆盖州法要求——实际上ESIGN Act第7001条本身也尊重州法对电子签名特定类型的排除规定。


### 5. 电子签名效力的边界与例外

**法规出处**：综合《47 C.F.R. § 54.1812》等条款及ESIGN Act定义【来源1】【来源2】【来源3】【来源5】

**深度解读**：上述FCC条款在赋予电子签名效力时，均以ESIGN Act的定义为基准。ESIGN Act虽未在所提供的资料中全文呈现，但从各条款的援引方式可推知：电子签名效力等同原则并非绝对，其适用范围受ESIGN Act自身例外条款的限制（如遗嘱、收养、离婚等特定文书类型）。在FCC通用服务项目语境下，主要涉及的是申请表、认证文件、合同等商业性文书，通常不属于ESIGN Act的排除范围。但需注意，各条款均使用"for the purposes of this [part]"的限定语，表明电子签名效力等同仅在FCC通用服务法规的目的范围内适用，不自动延伸至其他法律领域。

**重点提示**：电子签名效力等同不等于电子签名不可被质疑。在行政审查或争议程序中，当事人仍可对电子签名的真实性、签署意图或系统可靠性提出异议。此外，若电子签名涉及跨境交易，还需考虑外国法对电子签名的认可程度。

**实务指引**：建议企业在采用电子签名时，同步保留传统书面备份或采用可验证的第三方电子签名平台（如符合ESIGN Act和UETA的技术标准），以降低效力争议风险。对于高价值或高风险合同，可考虑在电子签名之外附加身份验证步骤（如视频见证或公证电子签名）。常见误区是认为"有电子签名就万无一失"——实际上证据链的完整性（谁签的、何时签的、签的什么内容）才是争议中的关键。


## 三、总结与建议

美国ESIGN Act通过FCC《47 C.F.R. § 54.1812》《§ 54.419》《§ 54.633》《§ 54.1612》等条款在通用服务领域落地，确立了**电子签名与书面签名效力等同、电子记录与纸质记录地位等同**的基本规则。核心要点有三：一是电子签名须以"签署意图"执行；二是电子记录须可追溯、可保存；三是效力等同仅在特定法规目的范围内适用，不排除其他法律的形式要求。

**行动指引**：参与FCC通用服务项目的实体应确保电子签名系统具备身份验证、时间戳和审计日志功能；电子记录管理应满足完整性和可读性要求；在电话营销场景中，电子同意还须符合州法标准。

**延伸提醒**：(1) 关注ESIGN Act与各州UETA的互动关系，州法可能对特定交易类型排除电子签名适用；(2) FCC各项目可能对记录保存期限有单独规定，电子记录须同步满足；(3) 跨境电子签名效力认定需结合交易准据法判断，不宜直接援引美国联邦规则。

## 一、核心概括

美国目前**没有针对人工智能的统一专门立法**，而是通过出口管制、通信牌照审查、政府合同知识产权等多条现有法律轨道"碎片化"监管AI相关技术与主体。核心抓手包括EAR对"技术/软件"的出口管辖、FCC对外国对手控制的持牌人审查，以及联邦采购中对技术数据的权利配置。以下逐条解读。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. EAR的"管辖范围"界定：AI技术是否"受EAR管辖"是监管起点

**法规出处**：美国《Export Administration Regulations》15 CFR §734.2【来源2】。

**深度解读**：§734.2(a)(1)明确，"Subject to the EAR"是描述BIS行使监管管辖权的**items and activities**的术语；反之，不受EAR管辖的物项和活动完全处于EAR监管之外。该条特别提示应查阅**商业管制清单（CCL）** 及EAR相关部分来判断某一物项或活动是否受管辖。对AI而言，这意味着：AI**软件、模型、技术数据**是否落入EAR管辖，取决于其是否属于EAR §734.2至§734.5、§734.9所描述的范围，而非"AI"这一标签本身。§734.2(a)(3)进一步强调，"受EAR管辖"**不等于**自动需要许可证——许可要求只在EAR其他部分明确施加时才产生。这一区分是实务中最易混淆之处。

**重点提示**：受EAR管辖的物项和活动**可能同时受其他出口相关管制项目约束**，§734.2(a)(2)明确要求企业注意可能需遵守**不止一个监管项目**，BIS与其他机构虽努力减少管辖重叠，但重叠客观存在。

**实务指引**：企业应建立"物项—活动"双重筛查流程：先判断AI技术/软件是否受EAR管辖（对照CCL与§734.2–734.5、§734.9），再判断是否触发具体许可要求；同时排查是否叠加其他管制项目。常见误区是将"开源"或"内部使用"直接等同于"不受管辖"。

### 2. "已发布"例外：公开AI技术与软件的豁免边界

**法规出处**：15 CFR §734.7【来源4】。

**深度解读**：§734.7(a)规定，除(b)(c)款例外，**非机密**的"技术"或"软件"在**无进一步传播限制**地向公众提供时即构成"published"，从而**不属于受EAR管辖的技术或软件**。列举情形包括：无限制订阅、公共图书馆馆藏、会议/展会无限分发、互联网公开张贴，以及向期刊合著者/审稿人、基础研究人员、开放会议组织者提交稿件。这对**公开发表的AI论文、公开模型权重、公开数据集**具有直接意义。

**重点提示**：§734.7(b)明确，**ECCN 5D002加密软件**即使公开仍受EAR管辖（除非满足§742.15(b)公开可用加密目标码条件）；§734.7(c)规定，用于生产**枪支及枪身/机匣**的软件或技术（ECCN 0A501、0A506、0A507、0A509）以电子格式上网发布仍受EAR管辖。AI企业若涉及加密模块或上述敏感领域，不能简单套用"已发布"豁免。

**实务指引**：主张"已发布"豁免须留存**公开发布的证据链**（发布渠道、无限制访问记录、分发范围）；对含加密功能的AI软件，须单独核查5D002及§742.15(b)；避免在发布时附加使用限制条款，否则可能破坏"无进一步传播限制"要件。

### 3. 基础研究例外：AI学术研究的监管安全港及其边界

**法规出处**：15 CFR §734.8【来源4】。

**深度解读**：§734.8(a)规定，在**基础研究**中产生或源于基础研究、且**意图发表**的技术或软件不受EAR管辖。§734.8(c)将"基础研究"定义为科学、工程或数学研究，其成果**通常发表**并在研究共同体中广泛共享，且研究人员**未接受**出于专有或国家安全原因的限制。§734.8(b)进一步明确：仅为确保**专利权**或防止泄露赞助方专有信息的**发表前审查**，只要仅造成**临时延迟**，仍视为"意图发表"。这对高校和企业的AI基础研究合规至关重要。

**重点提示**：§734.8(a) Note 1强调，该条**不适用于为开展基础研究而释放的、本身受EAR管辖的技术或软件**——即"输入"与"产出"须区分。Note 2指出，一旦决定对研究成果中的技术或软件**维持限制或专有**，且落入§734.3(a)范围，即**转为受EAR管辖**。Note 3明确，政府资助研究中**政府施加的特定国家安全管制**（如发表前审查并有权不予发表、限制向非美国公民传播）满足后，成果仍可认定为基础研究。

**实务指引**：AI研究机构应制定**发表政策**，确保发表前审查仅限于专利保护或赞助方专有信息，且延迟为临时性；对接受政府资助的项目，逐项识别是否存在"特定国家安全管制"；建立"限制决定"的书面记录机制，一旦转为专有即启动EAR合规评估。

### 4. FCC外国对手控制审查：AI相关通信持牌主体的准入与披露

**法规出处**：美国《Practice and Procedure (FCC)》47 CFR §1.80001、§1.80002【来源1】【来源5】。

**深度解读**：§1.80001(a)定义"Covered Authorization"为委员会授予并列入§1.80002附表范围的许可、租赁、授权等；§1.80001(e)将"由外国对手拥有、控制或受其管辖或指示"援引§1.70001(g)定义，并确立**10%表决权/股权推定规则**——委员会一般推定持有受监管主体10%及以上总流通表决权和/或股权的持有人**拥有决定、指导或决定重要事项的权力**，同时授权许可局与执法局**逐案例外**。§1.80002(a)-(c)以Schedule A/B/C对授权分类，涵盖无线、广播、空间站、海底电缆登陆、设备认证等，并设置雇员人数、外国赞助识别等限定条件。

**重点提示**：§1.80002(e)规定附表修改须经**通告评论规则制定**，并权衡国家安全风险、可管理性、受监管主体负担等标准；修改公告须给予**不少于生效后30日**的新 attestation 提交期限。AI企业若通过通信牌照、设备认证或数据网络识别码等开展业务，可能落入附表范围。

**实务指引**：涉及通信业务的AI企业应首先核查自身授权是否列入Schedule A/B/C；对**10%以上**的外国持股进行穿透核查，必要时申请逐案例外；关注附表更新公告及attestation截止日，建立股权变动触发复核机制。

### 5. 联邦采购中的技术数据权利：政府资助AI成果的权利配置

**法规出处**：美国《Technical Data and Associated Rights》48 CFR §227.7103-4【来源3】。

**深度解读**：该条规定政府对技术数据（含版权许可）取得**不可撤销许可**，承包商保留未授予政府的全部权利。许可范围一般由**开发资金来源**决定：完全私人出资开发的项目/部件/工艺，承包商可主张**有限权利（limited rights）** 限制政府使用、修改、发布等；完全政府出资则为**无限权利（unlimited rights）**；**混合出资**则为**政府目的权利（government purpose rights）**——政府内部可无限制使用，对外释放仅限政府目的。对不依附于项目/部件/工艺的技术数据（如概念设计），同样按资金来源确定权利范围。

**重点提示**：资金来源的确定应在**可行的子项或子部件层级**或工艺的可分割部分进行；承包商可就符合有限权利条件的**可分割子项、子部件或工艺部分**主张有限权利（依252.227-7013条款）。

**实务指引**：承接联邦AI研发合同的企業应在合同履行中**按子项/子部件粒度记录资金来源**，对私人出资部分及时主张有限权利；对混合出资成果，明确标注"government purpose rights"并建立对外释放审批流程；避免将不同资金来源的成果混同导致权利主张失败。

## 三、总结与建议

美国AI监管呈现**"无统一立法、多轨道并行"**的碎片化格局：EAR从**技术出口**维度管辖AI软件与技术数据，并以"已发布"和"基础研究"两项例外划定豁免边界；FCC从**通信持牌主体**维度审查外国对手控制，10%股权推定是核心风险点；联邦采购规则则从**资金溯源**维度配置AI成果的知识产权。三者相互独立又可能叠加适用。

**行动指引**：企业应建立跨法域的AI合规矩阵，按"技术属性—主体身份—资金来源"三条线索分别排查。

**延伸提醒**：其一，EAR §734.2(a)(2)提示多监管项目重叠，切勿以单一合规结论替代全面排查；其二，FCC附表处于动态更新中，须持续跟踪通告评论及attestation期限；其三，现有资料未涵盖美国各州层面AI立法及NIST AI风险管理框架等软法文件，如需评估州级合规义务，建议另行检索补充。
